overview: A storm trough crosses the Great Basin and Rockies in pieces through Saturday, with snow strongest in Utah and the northern Rockies. A second, weaker system follows the weekend, and a holiday-week system is still uncertain.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A storm moves in pieces from Thursday morning through Saturday morning, with the heaviest snow favoring the northern mountains. Southwest flow favors the upslope terrain. Snow levels stay above the valley floors until a cooler wave Friday evening brings valley snow into Saturday morning. Brighton leads with 39" total. Winter Weather Advisories run Thursday through Saturday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A strong storm brings heavy Sierra snow and gusty winds through Friday morning, with a brief dry spell after. Kirkwood leads with 39" total, and Mt. Rose has a Winter Storm Warning and an Avalanche Warning through Friday. Another system arrives Saturday afternoon, and the forecasters expect more active weather into Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: The same storm brings heavy snow to the Sierra through Friday morning, with strong winds over the ridges. A dry, cold break follows Friday afternoon through Saturday morning, then another system arrives Saturday afternoon. Mammoth leads with 27" total and has a Winter Storm Warning through Friday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Coastal storms bring mostly rain, with snow mainly at higher elevations. Snow picks up Tuesday and Wednesday. Cypress Mountain's chances are mostly rain through Tuesday. Whistler's snow chances rise late in the week, with Whistler leading at 23" total.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Clouds move in from Idaho, with snow showers on the western mountains through Friday. Winds are strongest in the eastern wind corridor. The forecasters expect Saturday, Sunday and Tuesday to be mostly dry, the best travel days of the holiday. Grand Targhee leads with 24" total.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: An upper low fades Friday, leaving dry and foggy mornings and clearing skies. A weak system brings light snow Saturday night into Sunday. A warm front Monday and a cold front Tuesday bring more snow to the mountains. Crystal Mountain leads with 17" total.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A storm brings measurable snow to the mountains from Thursday night through Saturday, with the moisture plume peaking Friday night. Snow chances return Monday. Telluride leads with 12" total. Temperatures drop as the weekend nears, and the forecasters say more fast-moving storms are possible in Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Strong winds hit the southern Sangres and eastern slopes Thursday night through Friday morning. Snow comes to the Continental Divide, with blowing snow on the high terrain. Light snow is possible Saturday and Monday. Wolf Creek leads with 10" total, and the NWS is calling for more, 7 to 17 inches Thursday night through Monday night.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center expects the next system to reach the Pacific Northwest and Intermountain West by Wednesday Nov 25, with more uncertainty on timing and strength after that.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
